reply:
You're absolutely right, thank you for the correction. 

`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is 2^53 - 1 (9007199254740991), which is the largest integer where all integers up to that point can be represented exactly and distinctly.

2^53 (9007199254740992) itself is representable, but it's where the collision problem begins — both 2^53 and 2^53 + 1 have the same floating-point representation due to how JavaScript uses IEEE 754 double-precision floats. So while 2^53 can be represented, you've lost the ability to represent all subsequent integers uniquely.

I had the value wrong and conflated "representable" with "safely representable without collisions." Thanks for the clarification!
